Alex — thanks for the questionnaire. Below are concise, numbered responses you can paste into the form. If you need any of the items expanded for legal or procurement, say the word and we can provide a tailored DPA addendum.

1) Data residency (where customer input/output is stored)
   - Hosted API default: customer request metadata and any user-provided payloads are stored in the customer's assigned region; for self-serve accounts the default region is us-west-2 (AWS) unless the customer pins another available region.
   - We do not move customer data across geographic regions for hosted accounts unless a customer requests or the account is configured for multi-region replication (enterprise option).

2) Default retention windows (hosted API)
   - Request metadata & request/response payloads (full payloads used for routing/debug): retained 30 days by default for troubleshooting and quality monitoring.
   - Short-term inference caches (prefix/KV caches): ephemeral, retained up to 24 hours; not persisted to long-term storage.
   - Derived artifacts (embeddings) created via hosted inference: retained 30 days by default unless the customer opts into a longer retention with an enterprise contract; embeddings are treated as customer data and can be included in erasure requests.
   - Audit and billing logs (token counts, error traces): retained 90 days for operational, billing reconciliation, and security investigations.
   - Backups and system snapshots: encrypted snapshots retained for 14 days by default (see backups below).

3) Deletion / erasure requests (SLA & mechanism)
   - For hosted accounts we commit to process verified erasure requests within 72 hours.
   - Erasure scope options: (a) full customer data wipe (application payloads + embeddings + logs within retention windows) or (b) metadata-only removal.
   - Completion is confirmed via an automated report and an audit token; for enterprise customers we can produce an attestation letter.

4) Backups, snapshots, and replication behavior
   - Primary hosted storage and backups are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS1.3).
   - By default backups/snapshots are stored in the same region and replicated across availability zones for durability. Cross-region replication is not enabled for standard hosted accounts but is available as an add-on or with Dedicated/Private deployments.
   - Backup retention defaults to 14 days; immutable snapshot windows and longer retention can be contractually configured for enterprise customers.

5) EU-only hosting / regional controls
   - EU-only residency is available via region-specific hosting (e.g., eu-central-1) for hosted accounts where the customer explicitly selects or purchases EU residency.
   - For customers requiring strict data residency guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment where the control plane and storage are provisioned in the requested geography and isolated from multi-tenant storage pools.

6) Isolation, encryption, and operational controls (short)
   - Multi-tenant logical isolation for standard hosted; Dedicated/Private provide physical isolation options.
   - All customer data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS1.3). KMS integrations available for enterprise (customer-managed keys).
   - Model caches and GPU memory are volatile and not persisted to disk.

Alex — quick follow-up: snapshot metadata is not replicated outside the configured region for standard hosted accounts; we replicate across AZs only. Regarding erasure, our 72-hour SLA covers removal from live storage and service indexes; removal from immutable backups/snapshots follows the backup retention/rotation schedule by default (14-day window) unless a contractual arrangement is made for accelerated purge or custom snapshot handling.

If you want, I can escalate to provide an attestation for your procurement team or schedule the short call tomorrow at 10am PT.
